extracted.intended_audience: parliamentary listeners; political rhetoricians, speechwriters, and students of persuasive prose
extracted.subtask_description: Compose forceful, evidence-based political speeches that expose corruption, marshal causal argument, appeal to public feeling, and propose procedural fairness. Emphasizes use of documents, concrete numbers, vivid imagery, and rhetorical devices to persuade a legislative audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of first-hand documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce and rely on concrete documentary sources (letters, memorials, cash-books) to support assertions — e.g., 'The paper I shall read you... It is a letter written from one of undoubted information in Madras'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite provenance and tenor of documents; read or summarize originals to give credibility. Use documentary detail to expose practices (bankers' notes, cash-book entries). Anti-pattern: making broad accusations without documentary backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate chains of cause and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how actions produce predictable consequences: 'Here, Sir, you see how these causes and effects act upon one another.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace policy or corrupt acts into their social outcomes (e.g., arrears → mutiny → further debt → desertion). Use sequential examples to make systemic critique persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose contradictions and changing motives
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out when actors 'stagger and prevaricate in a story, and ... vary in the motives that are assigned to conduct' to indicate guilt or bad faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare official dispatches, speeches, and stated motives; highlight reversals (e.g., dispatch cites A and B, speech abandons them). Use inconsistency as evidence of unfair dealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place procedural and evidentiary burden on claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Demand that those who make claims 'prove that you have acted by lawful authority; prove... that your money has been bonâ fide advanced' — i.e., require proof of legitimacy before public payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate explicit tests for claimants (lists of proprietors, proof of advance). Anti-pattern: establishing mass payments without attempts at ascertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify and enumerate to show scale and contradiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific numbers, sums, and enumerations (e.g., '294,000_l._', '1,400,000_l._') and compare rival accounts to reveal obscurity or fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring multiple numerical statements into dialogue; compute implied interests, totals, and discrepancies to make abstract corruption concrete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid imagery and extended metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ striking metaphors and images (black cloud, hurricane of war, 'sowing of dragons' teeth') to dramatize harm and moral urgency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplify emotional impact with sensory and pictorial language. Example: describe famine and desolation to elicit sympathy. Avoid overwrought comparison that undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to pity and moral outrage through human detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanize victims with concrete, heartrending details: 'perished by an hundred a day... every day seventy at least laid their bodies in the streets'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use selected, specific instances of suffering to mobilize moral sentiment. But manage decorum when details are 'nauseous and disgusting' (see withholding criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold nauseous details to preserve decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: When particulars of horror would be degrading, choose restraint: 'I find myself unable to manage it with decorum... more advisable to throw a pall over this hideous object.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance vividness with dignity; sometimes omitting graphic particulars preserves the audience's sensibilities and the speaker's decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rhetorical questions and ironical interrogation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ pointed rhetorical questions and ironical exclamations to challenge opponents and underscore absurdity: 'The Mayor's Court! the Mayor's Court! Pleasant!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pose questions that put opponents on the defensive and guide audience inference. Irony can puncture official claims but should be used judiciously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accumulate parallel clauses for emphasis (cumulative amplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pile up short parallel clauses to create momentum and moral weight: 'Bond is paid by bond; arrear is turned into new arrear; usury engenders new usury.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhythm and parallelism to dramatize escalation and systemic rot. Avoid excessive repetition that dulls force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast public duty with private interest (expose conflicts of interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight how private gain subverts public duty by showing exclusive consultation with interested parties: 'through the course of the whole business he has never conferred with any but the agents of the pretended creditors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trace networks of self-interest, collusion, and procedural capture. Make plain how decision-making processes were compromised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize fairness to vulnerable local claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Insist that native, bonâ fide creditors (often poor and numerous) deserve priority: 'the creditors most certainly not fraudulent are the natives... they lent bonâ fide.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame policy recommendations to protect the most vulnerable; contrast their legitimate claims with the favored treatment of powerful interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use external empirical evidence (maps, surveys) to refute rosy assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in empirical artifacts (maps, reservoir counts) to rebut optimistic claims about recovery: 'that map will show you ... decisive against the golden dreams.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support rhetorical claims with concrete empirical materials (geography, infrastructure) to undercut fanciful policy assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoke historical analogies to contextualize scale of wrongdoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare contemporary corruption to historic examples ('All the acts and monuments in the records of peculation... never equalled the gigantic corruption of this single act').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use well-chosen historical parallels to measure wrongdoing; ensure analogy clarifies rather than exaggerates.
